**The document doesn't contain the diagram's labels.** Figure 1 appears only as an image reference with a caption (p. 5). I can't read text inside the image, so I can't say which pooling operations it names. The text also never calls anything an "aggregated user embedding" or "visited-profile embeddings"; it uses "clicked profiles," "history embedding," and "final query representation."

The caption and text do describe the corresponding components:

- **History embedding from clicked-profile embeddings:** The history tower combines recent interaction embeddings using **positional attention** (P-ATT) (Figure 1 caption, p. 5). Equation 5 defines it as a softmax over a learned vector applied to each embedding plus a learned positional encoding, then a weighted sum (p. 5). This attention is deliberately query-agnostic (p. 5). It aggregates the K = 10 most recently clicked profiles (p. 5).
- **Final user/query representation:** This step is **normalized additive fusion**, not pooling. The profile and history embeddings are each L2-normalized, and the history embedding is scaled by a learnable scalar γ. They are then added and L2-normalized again (Equations 3–4, p. 5; Figure 1 caption, p. 5).

Max, mean, GeM, and plain attention pooling were tested only as alternative history aggregators in ablations. P-ATT scored best (MAR@100 0.450), with GeM close behind (0.447) (Table 2, p. 7).
